findings.title: Merged-PR comment helpers defined on CommitContextIntegration but called on PRCommentWorkflow, causing AttributeError
findings.body: The new static method `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` (along with `get_environment_info` and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` themselves) is added at the end of `CommitContextIntegration` — the diff places them immediately after `get_top_5_issues_by_count` and immediately before `class OpenPRCommentWorkflow(ABC):`. `PRCommentWorkflow` is a separate ABC that only composes an integration (`__init__(self, integration: CommitContextIntegration)`), so `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` does not exist and raises AttributeError the first time a merged-PR comment body is formatted. The same mismatch exists at the call sites: `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` now invoke `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` and `self.get_environment_info(...)` on workflow instances that do not inherit from `CommitContextIntegration`. Consequence: the merged-PR suspect-issues comment tasks for GitHub and GitLab crash instead of posting/updating the comment. Move the helpers onto `PRCommentWorkflow` (and fix the class referenced in the static call), or invoke them via `self.integration`.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) mis-pairs error IDs with event data from nodestore get_multi
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `ErrorEvent` objects with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id whose value order is whatever the backend returned (the Django backend uses an unordered `id__in` query, effectively lexicographic by node id, not the input order), and it omits entries for ids that have no stored event. As a result the i-th `error_id` is not guaranteed to correspond to the i-th value: titles, messages and timestamps get attached to the wrong error ids, and any single missing event shifts every subsequent pairing. The corrupted records are then sorted by the wrong `timestamp` and sent to Seer as the error context for the replay summary, so the summary can cite the wrong errors in the wrong chronological positions. The function already computes `node_ids`; it should look up each event explicitly (e.g. `events.get(node_id)` for each `(error_id, node_id)` pair) instead of relying on `.values()` ordering.

findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty columns and data
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, the `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{ data: [], meta: { fields: {}, units: {} } }} />` — literal empty columns and empty data — while ignoring the real query results (`result.data`, `fields`, `result.meta`, `fieldAliases`) that are computed immediately above and still feed the `StyledSimpleTableChart` fallback. As soon as the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is turned on for an organization, every table widget on that organization's dashboards renders an empty table with no headers and no rows. This reads as an unfinished stub that slipped in: either wire the actual table results into `TableWidgetVisualization` or keep rendering `StyledSimpleTableChart` until the new path is implemented.

findings.title: "Project not found" error flashes while projects are still loading
findings.body: The new guard `if (replayRecord?.project_id && !project)` renders an error alert ("Project not found. Unable to load AI summary.") whenever `useProjectFromId` returns undefined. However `useProjectFromId` also returns undefined while the projects store is still loading, so on any visit where projects are not already cached the user briefly (or, on a slow load, persistently) sees a false error state instead of the loading spinner that the previous code fell through to. The error branch should be gated on the projects store having finished loading (e.g. check `initiallyLoaded` from `useProjects`) so it only fires when the project genuinely cannot be found.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators bypassable with a 0 value
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` are meant to enforce that a report contains either `age` (Editor's Draft) or `timestamp` (Working Draft), never both, but they check presence via truthiness: `if self.initial_data.get("age")` / `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A report containing both fields passes validation whenever one of them is `0` (e.g. `age: 0` alongside a `timestamp`), because `0` is falsy, defeating the mutual-exclusion rule the endpoint explicitly documents in the serializer comments. Use a real presence check such as `"age" in self.initial_data` (or `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None`) so zero values cannot bypass the constraint.
